chunks: He exhorted the people: O people,
secure light from the flame of the lamp of the preacher who follows what he preaches and draw water from the spring which has been cleaned of dirt.
O creatures of Allāh, do not rely on your ignorance, do not be obedient to your desires

because he who stays at this place is like one who stays on the brink of a bank undermined by water carrying ruin on his back from one portion to the other following his opinion which he changes (one after the other).
He wants to make adhere what cannot adhere and to bring together what cannot keep together.
ai.seo_question: What is the warning against following personal desires in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this eloquent sermon from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) urges the community to seek authentic guidance from those who embody wisdom, contrasting them with the Umayyads who are depicted as unstable and driven by base desires. He employs the vivid metaphor of standing on the edge of a precipice to illustrate the precariousness of those whose shifting opinions fail to cohere, warning that their reliance on ignorance leads inevitably to ruin. This passage underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawhid* of leadership and the necessity of following the *Ahl al-Bayt* as the pure, stable source of divine knowledge amidst political turmoil.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [About the functions of the Imams :] O people,
secure light from the flame of lamps of the preacher who follows what he preaches and draw water from the spring which has been cleaned of dirt.
O creatures of Allāh, do not rely on your ignorance, do not be obedient to your desires

because he who stays at this place is like one who stays on the brink of a bank undermined by water carrying ruin on his back from one portion to the other following his opinion which he changes (one after the other).
He wants to make adhere what cannot adhere and to bring together what cannot keep together.
